r1.name: Fortified Rice
r1.description: Iron-fortified rice distributed through PDS reaches households directly and is culturally accepted across all regions.

r2.name: Jaggery (Gur)
r2.description: Traditional jaggery contains non-heme iron and is widely available, affordable, and culturally embedded across rural India.

r3.name: Dried Lentils (Masoor Dal)
r3.description: Lentils are a high-iron legume with long shelf life, storable without refrigeration, and central to existing food habits.

r4.name: Drumstick Leaves (Moringa)
r4.description: Moringa leaves are exceptionally rich in iron and can be grown locally; limited shelf life is a distribution challenge.

r5.name: Vitamin A Supplementation Capsules
r5.description: Biannual Vitamin A supplementation through ASHA workers is the most direct, clinically validated intervention for severe deficiency.

r6.name: Sweet Potato (Orange Flesh)
r6.description: Orange-fleshed sweet potato is a biofortified crop with high beta-carotene, suitable for home gardening programs.

r7.name: Carrot & Leafy Vegetable Mix
r7.description: Seasonal vegetable mixes high in carotenoids; best distributed fresh through Anganwadi centres for maximum potency.

r8.name: Fortified Edible Oil
r8.description: Vitamin A-fortified edible oil integrates into cooking without behavior change and has long shelf life.

r9.name: Zinc-ORS Supplementation
r9.description: Zinc-ORS combination tablets are recommended for children under 5 during diarrhoea episodes and as a preventive supplement.

r10.name: Sesame Seeds (Til)
r10.description: Sesame seeds are a high-zinc food with excellent shelf life, available year-round, and used in traditional snacks (chikki).

r11.name: Pumpkin Seeds
r11.description: Pumpkin seeds are zinc-dense with a neutral flavour and can be added to existing snack distributions.

r12.name: Iodised Salt (Double Fortified)
r12.description: Double-fortified iodised salt (iron + iodine) is the most cost-effective, scalable intervention for iodine deficiency.

r13.name: Iodine Supplementation Drops
r13.description: Iodine drops administered via health workers for areas where iodised salt uptake remains low.

r14.name: Folic Acid Tablets (IFA Programme)
r14.description: Weekly IFA tablets distributed through government WIFS programme to adolescent girls and women — high coverage, low cost.

r15.name: Fortified Wheat Flour (Atta)
r15.description: Folate-fortified atta distributed through PDS integrates with existing food distribution with no additional behavior change.

r16.name: Green Leafy Vegetables Bundle
r16.description: Spinach, methi, and amaranth are high in folate; best distributed fresh near source through Anganwadi or kitchen gardens.
